## Model Construction
```{r}
# Take a representative 20% sample
set.seed(123)
model_sample <- final_model_data %>% sample_frac(0.1)

# Prepare matrices from the sample
Y <- as.numeric(model_sample$y_count)
W <- as.numeric(model_sample$treatment)
X <- model_sample %>% 
     select(baseline_risk, y_coord, dist_60th, week_index) %>% 
     as.matrix()

# Train the Local Linear Causal Forest
# This fits a local linear regression in each leaf—perfect for the 60th St boundary
# Training with progress
cf_final <- causal_forest(X, Y, W, 
                          num.trees = 1000, 
                          clusters = model_sample$hex_id,
                          tune.parameters = "all") 
# Cluster by Hex to account for spatial correlation

# Predict the CATE (The 'Impact' for each row)
# We use the MEDIAN week_index (the middle of the study) for the spatial map



# 1. Identify the 'Post-Treatment' weeks only
post_treatment_weeks <- model_sample$week_index[model_sample$treatment == 1]

# 2. Find the median of JUST those weeks
target_week <- median(post_treatment_weeks)

# 3. Update X_map with this relevant timestamp
X_map <- model_sample %>%
  distinct(hex_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(week_index = target_week) %>% 
  select(baseline_risk, y_coord, dist_60th, week_index) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Predict on Matrix of Hexagons
predictions_map <- predict(cf_final, 
                           newdata = X_map,
                           linear.correction.variables = 1:4,
                           estimate.variance = TRUE) # This shows the IJ variance progress

# Calculate the Average Treatment Effect (ATE)
average_treatment_effect(cf_final, target.sample = "treated")

# P Value
test_calibration(cf_final)
```
# Policy Impact Visualization
```{r}

# Join Predictions to Grid
hex_grid$tau_hat <- predictions_map$predictions

hex_impact <- hex_features %>%
  mutate(
    tau = predictions_map$predictions,
    # Calculate the 95% Confidence Interval to check significance
    se = sqrt(predictions_map$variance.estimates),
    t_stat = tau / se,
    is_significant = abs(t_stat) > 1.96
  ) %>%
  select(hex_id, tau, is_significant)

# Join to the spatial hexagons
plot_data <- hex_grid %>%
  left_join(hex_impact, by = "hex_id")

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(plot_data) +
  geom_sf(data = nyc_boundary, fill = "#f0f0f0", color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = tau), color = NA) + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166ac", 
    mid = "#f7f7f7", 
    high = "#b2182b", 
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Change in\nWeekly Collisions"
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 217000, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 985000, y = 220000, label = "60th St Toll Boundary", size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  # --- ADD: This locks the view to the actual city limits ---
  coord_sf(xlim = st_bbox(nyc_boundary)[c(1,3)], 
           ylim = st_bbox(nyc_boundary)[c(2,4)]) +
  theme_void() + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "right", # Move legend to the side for now to see everything
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Causal Impact of Congestion Pricing on Traffic Safety",
    subtitle = "Estimated via Local Linear Causal Forest (N = 1.72M)",
    caption = "Data: NYPD Motor Vehicle Collisions | EPSG:2263"
  )
```
